Secure or complete your secondary school diploma by 10 July 2026.

Budget for the EUR 156.00 regional tax and stamp duty, which the tuition waiver does not cover.

Failing to name an undergraduate programme from the Annex 1 list.

Visa, travel and insurance costs to Italy.

Secondary school diploma, or a written commitment that it will be completed by 10 July 2026.
Transcripts evidencing 12 years of schooling, or the extra year of post-secondary education with all exams passed.
Statement of the chosen Annex 1 undergraduate degree programme.

eligibility: Open to individuals of any age and nationality.
Must hold, by 31 October 2026, a second-cycle degree (laurea specialistica and/or magistrale, a single-cycle degree, or an equivalent qualification under the pre-Ministerial Decree 509/99 system).
Candidates who obtain the qualifying degree between submission of the application and 31 October 2026 are admitted 'with reserve' until they obtain it.

Those who already hold a PhD degree obtained without a scholarship may apply provided the predominant research topics and scientific-disciplinary sectors of the intended programme differ from those of the programme for which the title was already obtained.
Candidates who are already enrolled in a previous PhD year without a scholarship may apply only within the number of non-scholarship positions announced, according to ranking order.

new_scholarship.description: The Taiwan Scholarship Program of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Republic of China (Taiwan), funds international students for degree programmes or a pre-degree Mandarin Language Enrichment Program at Mandarin-teaching institutions affiliated with MOE-accredited universities. Recipients receive a monthly stipend of NT$33,000 for degree programmes or NT$28,000 for the LEP, plus one-way economy-class air tickets for direct flights to and from Taiwan, and must cover all other expenses themselves. The award period is one year for the LEP, up to four years for undergraduate and doctoral study and two years for a master's, with a five-year total cap. Applications are accepted from 1 February to 31 March each year, and the programme is open to students of any country except mainland China, Hong Kong and Macau, in principle prioritising Taiwan's diplomatic partners.

programme_detail_official.description: The Taiwan International Graduate Program, administered by Academia Sinica with partner universities, admits international students to fourteen English-taught Ph.D. programmes. Admitted students receive a tax-free stipend of NT$40,000 per month (NT$34,000 + NT$6,000) for the first year, extended for one further year for good performers, and Academia Sinica subsidises the international tuition surcharge for five consecutive years, after which students still pay domestic tuition of roughly NT$28,000-31,000 per semester for the first four semesters and NT$16,000-20,000 thereafter. Applications are submitted online with no application fee between 1 November and 1 February GMT+8, and results are usually announced in late June or early July for the following fall enrolment.

programme_detail_official.coverage: Tax-free stipend of NT$40,000 per month for the first year, extendable one further year; full subsidy of the international tuition differential for five consecutive years, leaving the student at the domestic tuition rate; optional separate fellowships and travel grants. Accommodation, food, insurance and tuition itself remain the student's own cost.

application_readiness_checklist: Choose one of the fourteen TIGP Ph.D. programmes and read that programme's own admissions requirements before applying.
Prepare your application for the 1 November to 1 February GMT+8 window; the site posts a cycle-specific announcement each November.
Submit through the TIGP online application system at https://tigp.apps.sinica.edu.tw/index.php - no application fee is charged.
Have academic records ready for the qualification you declare; add any programme-specific documents.

Budget for domestic-rate tuition: roughly NT$28,000-31,000 per semester for the first four semesters and NT$16,000-20,000 per semester thereafter. The international surcharge is subsidised, tuition itself is not.
Plan how you will select a thesis advisor before the end of your first year, because post-stipend support depends on that advisor.
Treat the stipend as a two-year maximum core award (first year, plus one extension for good performance) and build a funding plan for year three.
Check whether you are also eligible for the Presidential, Research Performance or Rising Star Fellowships, or for travel grants.
Contact the programme secretary directly for the tuition figure that applies to your specific programme.
common_rejection_risks: Missing the 1 February GMT+8 deadline - TIGP's window is only three months and there is no stated grace period.
Applying to a programme whose own admission requirements you have not met.
Assuming TIGP pays full tuition: it subsidises the international differential only, and domestic tuition remains payable.
Assuming the stipend lasts the full three years: it is first year plus one extension for good performers, then advisor-dependent.
Not contacting the programme secretary, which is TIGP's stated route for programme-specific tuition costs.
Overlooking academic integrity expectations; TIGP states violations can affect grades, stipend and academic standing.
estimated_uncovered_costs: Domestic-rate tuition: approximately NT$28,000-31,000 per semester for the first four semesters and NT$16,000-20,000 per semester for the remainder until graduation.
Accommodation: approximately NT$5,000-14,000 per month (on-campus dormitory around NT$5,500; Taipei off-campus single room NT$5,000-14,000).
Books, National Health Insurance, transport and recreation: approximately NT$1,000-3,000 per month.
Airfare to Taiwan, and all costs after the stipend allowance period if the thesis advisor does not provide support.

alerts.message: Academia Sinica subsidises only the international fee differential for five consecutive years. Students pay the domestic rate: roughly NT$28,000-31,000 per semester for the first four semesters and NT$16,000-20,000 per semester after that. Do not treat TIGP as full tuition funding.

alerts.message: The TIGP Scholarship/Stipend page states NT$40,000 per month (NT$34,000 + NT$6,000) for the first year, extended one further year for good performers. TIGP's FAQ also refers to a 'full fellowship for up to three years' with an NT$34,000 stipend extended 'for a further 2 to 3 years'. Confirm the current terms with tigp@as.edu.tw before relying on either figure for a three-year budget.

As of 2026-10-04 TIGP had not posted its next application announcement. The standing window is 1 November to 1 February GMT+8; check the News & Announcement page for the dated announcement when it appears.
TIGP also runs the Taiwan International Internship Program (TIIP), a separate non-degree scheme with its own selection phases. Do not apply for both on the same basis.

submission_workflow: Read the TIGP admissions page and the requirements for your chosen Ph.D. programme.
Prepare transcripts, degree evidence and any programme-specific documents during the summer and autumn.
Watch the TIGP News & Announcement page from 1 November for the dated application announcement for the coming cycle.
Submit through the TIGP online application system before 1 February GMT+8.
Complete any programme-level assessment, research proposal submission or interview.
Await the ranking, normally announced in late June or early July.
On admission, confirm tuition with the programme secretary, enrol at the partner university, and begin advisor selection in your first year.
